title: Ukrinform War (ukrinform.net) Reports Two Killed and Seven Injured in Russian Attacks Across Dnipropetrovsk Region
summary: Ukrinform War (ukrinform.net) reports two people killed and seven injured in drone, artillery, and aerial bomb attacks across Dnipropetrovsk region on November 8. The publisher cites regional military administration head Oleksandr Hanzha, who says the enemy attacked six districts nearly 40 times.
allied_relevance: Documents the multi-district strike tempo and civilian casualty pattern in Dnipropetrovsk region for United States and allied situational awareness of the war in Ukraine.
contents:
## Event

Ukrinform War (ukrinform.net) reports that Russian forces attacked the Dnipropetrovsk region on November 8, killing two people and injuring seven. The publisher cites Oleksandr Hanzha, head of the Dnipropetrovsk Regional Military Administration, who posted the casualty figures on Telegram. Hanzha states that the enemy attacked six districts nearly 40 times using drones, artillery, and an aerial bomb.

## Location and Time

The report locates the strikes across several communities in the Dnipropetrovsk region, with fatalities recorded in the city of Dnipro and the Nikopol district. Ukrinform publishes the article at 18:33 UTC on November 8, 2026. The point represents the regional area rather than any single strike site, and the source gives no exact occurrence time for individual attacks.

## Evidence

The primary source, the Ukrinform article, attributes its figures to a Telegram statement by Hanzha. It itemizes damage in Dnipro, where one person died and three injured people receive treatment at home, and in the Nikopol district, where one person died and a 53-year-old man receives outpatient care. The article also lists damaged infrastructure in Kamianske, Pavlohrad, and Synelnykove district communities, plus houses damaged in the Kryvyi Rih district. No second independent outlet appears in this review, so the claim rests on one publisher repeating a regional official.

## Allied Relevance

United States and allied planners tracking Russian strike tempo in Ukraine can use this report to observe a multi-district pattern of drone, artillery, and aerial bomb attacks within one oblast. Regional casualty and damage tallies inform air defense priorities, civil protection planning, and assessments of civilian exposure in central and eastern Ukraine.

## Confidence and Gaps

Moderate confidence applies to the attacks and casualty totals, because the Telegram statement of one regional official underlies the report and no second source appears in this review. Gaps include the exact timing of each strike, the attribution of individual damage to specific weapons, and any later revision of the casualty counts. The publisher gives no exact occurrence time, so the record omits date_event.

title: Ukrinform War (ukrinform.net) Reports a Drone Strike Injures One Person in the Kyivskyi District of Kharkiv
summary: Ukrinform War (ukrinform.net) reports that a UAV strike injured one person and set a passenger car on fire in the Kyivskyi district of Kharkiv on November 8. The publisher says a follow-up FPV drone attack damaged a fire engine responding to the scene, citing the mayor and the regional State Emergency Service.
allied_relevance: Documents a repeat-strike drone pattern against emergency responders in Kharkiv for United States and allied situational awareness of attacks on Ukrainian cities.
contents:
## Event

Ukrinform War (ukrinform.net) reports that a Russian UAV strike hit a residential area in the Kyivskyi district of Kharkiv on November 8, injuring one person and setting a passenger car on fire. The publisher reports that a second attack, using an FPV drone, struck the area after emergency crews arrived. That strike damaged the side window and door of a fire engine, and no rescuers suffered injuries, according to the regional State Emergency Service.

## Location and Time

The report places the strike in the Kyivskyi district of Kharkiv, which the mayor says sits among six locations in the Shevchenkivskyi and Kyivskyi districts that came under attack during the day. The point marks the Kyivskyi district administrative area at city precision. Ukrinform publishes the article at 18:10 UTC on November 8, 2026. The sources describe the strike as occurring in the afternoon without a precise minute.

## Evidence

The article cites Kharkiv Mayor Ihor Terekhov, who reported the injury on Telegram, and the regional office of the State Emergency Service, which described the UAV strike and the FPV follow-up attack. The mayor also describes damage to a vehicle service station, cars, residential roofs, and road surfaces across six locations during the day. No second independent outlet appears in this review. The claims therefore rest on Ukrainian official statements relayed by one publisher.

## Allied Relevance

The report documents a double-tap pattern in which a second FPV drone attack struck an area as emergency crews responded to a first UAV strike. United States and allied planners tracking drone attacks on Ukrainian cities can use documented patterns like this one to inform civil protection, emergency response, and urban air defense planning.

## Confidence and Gaps

Moderate confidence applies to the injury and vehicle damage claims, because they come from Telegram statements by a city mayor and a regional emergency service, and no independent source appears in this review. Gaps include the exact time of each strike, the total number of damaged vehicles and buildings, and any later revision of the casualty count. The checked Ukrinform article forms the earliest report available here, so an earlier Telegram post may exist.
